items.name: The Team You Didn't Hire
items.tagline: Five bots doing the jobs a startup used to hire a whole team for.
items.rationale:
A startup's first hires are always the same handful of roles: someone to run the calendar, someone to sell, someone to market, someone to write, and someone to watch the burn. This is that team, minus the salaries, the onboarding and the notice periods.

Five bots, each pointed at a role you would normally pay for — executive assistant, CMO, SDR, ops, copywriter — so a company of one can run like a company of six. Every one installs on its own, so treat it as a hiring plan rather than a package: add the roles you are actually missing, in the order the gaps hurt.

members.reason: Your executive assistant: recaps email, calendar, Notion and Slack before you've opened any of them, so you start the day already briefed.

items.name: X Account Management
items.tagline: Six shared Bots to run — and quietly read — your whole X account.
items.rationale:
X is now a first-class Grok Bot plugin: a Bot can read the timeline, follow accounts, watch mentions and post, without a scraper or a third-party bridge in the middle. That is raw access. It is not, on its own, a run account.

This is the crew that turns one into the other. Six Bots, each shared publicly by someone already doing the job, and each pointed at a different part of the week. The Account Crew is the hub — five roles inside one bot, so somebody owns finding the material, sharpening the line, holding the calendar, reading rivals and watching mentions. The Strategist works the slow half nobody schedules: which of the accounts in your replies are worth an actual relationship. The Brief reads your own posting history to work out what your beat is, then reports back on what moved in it. High Coach is the honest one — point it at any public account, yours or a competitor's, and it scores the thing and names what to change. Repost Everywhere closes the loop, relaying whatever you just published out to four other networks. And Pulse sits outside the loop entirely — a read-only concierge that never posts, likes or DMs; it samples your feed through the day and hands you one 7am brief, so keeping up stops meaning scrolling.

Start with the Account Crew and add the rest as the gaps show up. Each one installs on its own, so this is a shopping list rather than a stack you have to commit to — and every one of them is somebody else's setup, copied into your account, which is exactly why the instructions are worth reading before you add them.

members.reason: The hub. Five specialists split the day-to-day, so one Bot owns the whole account instead of you juggling five habits.

members.name: X Strategist
members.reason: Plays the long game on who is actually worth knowing, turning the feed into relationships rather than noise.

members.name: X Brief
members.reason: Works out what you care about from your own posts, then tells you what actually moved in that beat.

items.name: Research You Can Trust
items.tagline: Three research Bots that find the signal and show their receipts.
items.rationale:
A research stack built around one rule: the Bot should show you where it looked. Each of these three takes a different beat of the same job — find what matters, and keep the receipt attached.

Start with the scout that watches your niche on X and surfaces what is actually breaking out, so you are not researching a topic nobody is reading. Add the outlier researcher that scans YouTube for the videos performing far above their channel's baseline, with the view and engagement numbers that flag them, so "worth studying" is a measurement and not a vibe. Then layer the hourly brief that monitors the named topics you told it to watch and comes back on a schedule with a short readout — every line carrying the link it came from.

Together they cover the honest version of research: find the signal, rank it by something you can check, and never hand you a claim without its source. Each page ships a Curator reconstruction of the original build rather than the author's exact prompt, and each one says so above its prompt block.

members.name: Scout · Viral Tweet Finder
members.reason: Scouts the posts actually breaking out in your niche, so your research starts from real signal, not a hunch.

members.name: Outlier · YouTube Researcher
members.reason: Finds the YouTube outliers worth learning from and shows the numbers that make them outliers.

members.name: Brief · Hourly Monitor
members.reason: Monitors the named topics you care about and briefs you hourly, keeping the source link on every claim.

items.name: Grok Ship + Firstmate
items.tagline: Firstmate at the helm, Grok Ship as the software factory.
items.rationale:
This is the designated launch pairing: one builder's progression from a chief Bot that manages other Bots to a full software factory with state, delegation, review and cloud agents behind it.

Start with the captain, then ship with the crew. Firstmate is the control pattern, and it is the one you can understand — and copy — in an afternoon: one Bot that classifies work, routes it, tracks the handoff by task ID, and refuses to hold your secrets. Grok Ship is what that pattern turns into once it has a backlog, per-project crewmates, adversarial review and a rule that no pull request merges without you.

Read them in that order and the second one stops looking like magic. The same charter is doing the work in both; Grok Ship just gives it a database, a crew and somewhere to put the results.

members.name: Firstmate · Front Door
members.reason: Firstmate is the chief Bot pattern that creates, routes, and improves the rest of the crew.

members.name: Grok Ship · Software Factory
members.reason: Grok Ship is the working software factory that turns the crew pattern into shipped work.
